title: Ada and the Vow
premise: Odile Brightwater has spent ten years exchanging anonymous letters with a stranger who signed only 'A'—letters that kept her sane through culinary school, her mother's death, and the slow collapse of her café. When Rowan Adeyemi, the letter-writer all along, moves in next door under a new lease and an old vow to finally reveal themselves, Odile must confront that the voice she trusted most belongs to someone she's been pushing away in person. As the café's final payment deadline collides with a career-saving offer that would take Odile across the country, she learns Rowan once chose duty over truth by staying silent about a betrayal that nearly ruined her family. In the end, Odile declines the offer, signs the café over to a cooperative of regulars rather than lose it entirely, and writes one last letter—to Rowan, delivered by hand, choosing loyalty to truth over the safe distance she swore by.
about_author: Ivo Oyelaran is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, laundromats, and other places where people can't hide what they feel. They live between Lagos and Lisbon and answer every letter they receive.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Three missed payments from losing Brightwater's café, Odile works dawn-to-midnight and recites her creed: the heart is trainable muscle. A moving truck arrives next door; its occupant, Rowan, helps carry flour up her stairs and feels unsettlingly familiar. Emotional beat: brittle control cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Letters We Kept
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rowan moved here on purpose, carrying a decade of unsent confessions and one old vow to come clean. Neighboring Odile means small kindnesses—fixed awning, borrowed sugar—that deepen the lie of anonymity. Rowan discovers the betrayal from years ago still shadows Odile's finances. Emotional beat: guilt sweetening into longing.

chapters.title: What the Yeast Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile finds Rowan's box of letters while returning a casserole dish—and recognizes her own words quoted back at her. The confrontation detonates: ten years of trust, and the silence about who let her family's bakery fail. That same night, the cross-country job offer arrives. Emotional beat: climax; love and fury indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Delivered by Hand
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the café's final deadline day, Odile chooses neither rescue offered outright: she converts the shop to a workers' co-op and turns down the offer. She writes one last letter, walks it next door, and knocks. Rowan opens the door before she can leave it. Emotional beat: resolution; truth chosen over safety, together.
